newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse opens firmer but dollar weighs.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse opens firmer but dollar weighs.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse started slightly firmer on Tuesday, with encouragement coming from a record close on Wall Street overnight and firmer Bunds.
But dealers said a lower dollar was weighing on German exporters, most notably in the chemicals and auto sectors.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares, was slightly up, rising 4.02 points, or 0.15 percent, to 2,732.34 points by 1043 GMT.
The dollar, which had lost a pfennig on Monday, continued to slip on Tuesday, approaching the 1.49 mark level, but then stablised around 1.495 marks.
"The Bund and the dollar are our main influences at the moment," said one trader.
Dealers said although the market was currently suffering from dollar weakness, the longer term outlook was still positive. "The market is very robust at the moment," said one trader.
The banking sector supported the market as German Bund strength gave it a boost.
Commerzbank was up 27 pfennigs at 34.60 marks, while Germany's biggest bank Deutsche Bank gained over one percent, or 1.12 marks to 69.37 marks.
Dealers said Deutsche Bank was boosted after the Oslo Stock Exchange said its investment arm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was not obliged to bid for the Norwegian software company Sysdeco Group.
Consumer products group Henkel KGAA was up 20 pfennigs at 72.00 marks, after it announced nine month figures in line with expectations.

Sportware manufacturer Adidas jumped in pre-bourse dealings to a high of 137 marks after it published its nine month results, but reaction to the figures then calmed down and the stock was up 1.50 marks at 134 marks in bourse trade.

Meanwhile the world's largest reinsurer Munich Re continued to fall on the back of a statement made on Monday that the company could see a fall in profits for the 1996/97 financial year. The stock was down 45 marks at 3,685 marks.
Munich Re shares were also under pressure from a downgrade by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to "neutral" from "overweight".
